title: Lost functionality after upgrade.
text:
Bear was absolutely perfect before the 2.0 update. 

There was a very slim/narrow bar along the top of the keyboard with all the functions. You had to slide it to get to some of them, but after 30 minutes’ use, it wasn’t a big deal. Plus it stayed in place when you slid it so you could generally complete what you were doing without much need for other items, anyway. And when you got used to it, it was extremely quick and easy to get to what you needed, practically like typing. 

Now they have turned that super functional bar into a gigantic second keyboard. You have to press a button to get to it, and then it obscures the keyboard entirely. Sure, you can press one button and make yourself a long to do list. But if you want to add any indentations? Change any headings? You have to shift into that screen, then shift back into the keyboard, continue the list, and then to go back to left alignment, you have to repeat the process. And so on and so forth for every single formatting event you want to make. 

It has destroyed the functionality of it for me. I had previously switched completely over to Bear from Apple Notes for the added functionality and being cleaner to look at it. As soon as the update came out, I switched back. I occasionally try to use bear again, but it has become clunky and frustrating. I use screens because I type faster than I can write. Unfortunately Bear 2.0 slows down the process so that when using it, I go slower than I can write.

I appreciate the developers’ desire to listen to and improve based on users’ feedback. I wish those new systems would be made optional (as in choose your system/interface) or togglable (as in switch on or off what you like). I have paid for at least a couple years now and would have paid more. I’m sure others like the new design so try it out yourself and don’t let this review sway you.

title: Quality App Uses Atypical Organization
text:
Bear is a nicely designed app that uses an unusual tagging structure for file organization. I think it will work well for many users looking for an Apple Notes replacement that uses plain text however, certain design decisions make it unusable for me. 

Bear doesn’t use a traditional hierarchy of directories for note organization but instead uses a tagging system that includes the option for nesting. Unfortunately, Bear doesn’t offer the ability to filter on multiple tags at once, which is to say constructing a query as simple as “tag1 AND tag2 AND tag3” can’t be handled in the UI without writing a string query. That’s a dealbreaker for me. 

It’s not exactly fair to judge Bear on this, but the general community opinion of the feature I’m describing seems to be negative, so I don’t expect it to be added.

title: Nice UI, horrible UX
text:
Overall, the app presents a visually appealing and thoughtfully designed aesthetic. However, from a functionality standpoint, the experience is significantly lacking. During my evaluation on an iPad, I found the process of attaching photos to a note to be particularly frustrating. The method for adding images from the photo library is far from intuitive—I had to resort to searching google for instructions, which reflects a serious shortcoming in the app’s user experience.

I previously used Bear regularly a couple of years ago and recently decided to revisit it. Unfortunately, it falls short when compared to Apple Notes, both in terms of usability and overall value. The interface feels unnecessarily complicated, and its lack of intuitiveness is a major barrier to productivity. While the app performs well for basic note-taking, any attempt to go beyond that requires external help, which should not be the case in a well-designed product.

There is clear potential here, but the current user experience leaves much to be desired. I strongly recommend investing in more thorough UX research and usability testing to better align the interface with users’ expectations and workflows.

title: Ho-hum
text:
Positives: an elegantly designed and presented app. 

Negatives: syncing is poorly implemented, bordering on half-baked. I'm syncing between two Macs, an iPad and an iPhone. Some notes simply don't sync at all; on both iPad and iPhone, images in notes don't appear. 

Preferences/settings are minimal so there's no way of manually initiating a sync. It may be automatic, but if one can't trust the sync, one can't trust the app. 

Finally, this requires an annual subscription for iCloud syncing and themes. Given that iCloud syncing is an Apple-provided technology the fact that these guys are charging is a disgrace. 

I've seen a few people talking about this being 1) an Evernote killer; 2) a Ulysses killer. On the first point, Bear handles attachments and webpage rendering more poorly than Apple Notes does, so if it can't kill Notes it's hardly worrying Evernote. Evernote is hideous, so I await a proper app into which I can import my old Evernote library. 

Anyone who thinks this is a Ulysses killer is an idiot, having been duped by the superficial likeness of the apps. Ulysses is better-designed with a rock-solid syncing backend. It is also has infinitely superior document management (by which I mean it actually has document management) and export options. But to be fair to the Bear guys, they don't mention Ulysses so the comparison is unfair. 

I'm giving it until the end of my free month to see if an update improves the performance of this app, but at this stage, I'm afraid it's hype over substance. Ho-hum.

title: Limited and even broken
text:
Markdown as a standard is a widely used syntax that Bear slightly expands upon with their use of tags so as to support inter-linking what you write. Supporting whitespace by wrapping text between #two hashtags# is a welcome innovative idea. But the welcome changes end there.

Bear locks down images into iCloud storage but in such a way that you cannot actually access them. Bear also provides weak image manipulation tools which do not include cropping. This extends into the drawing tool, where canvas size is automatically chosen by wherever a stroke may have landed. In other words, you could draw a lovely image but it could be uselessly and awkwardly bordered by whitespace, often shoved in a corner. I think they expect users to use the whole canvas every time which is stupid to assume.

Then there are the export options that are still severely lacking. Many static site generators rely on markdown and are thirsty for an application like Bear so that simple blogs can be maintained. Git integration is not an option. Again, flat file storage for images is not an option. Even on Desktop, you are locked in to only working on iCloud which means you can’t get to work on a regular folder of text files. That’s pretty lame in my opinion!

I want to like Bear, but it always feels broken in these ways.

Having been a developer myself, I simply cannot understand why it is so hard for these devs to create a simple search function which has been requested over and over by hundreds of bear users. It certainly wouldn’t take lot of coding knowledge to add this basic feature so again I cannot understand why they still can’t seem to figure it out after years have come and went. That being said, I regret to say that my patience has worn thin and I can longer just hope that the issue will eventually be resolved. title: Usefull yet deceiving
text:
The app offers a multitute of different options and programs, while accompanied with a charming easy to navigate interface.

Some of the offered programs are challenges to reduce coffee intake, alcohol intake, or even overly sweet drinks,
you can also messure these out in your daily liquid intake, even better with the help of a widget.
Or different cosmetics to spice up the users experience.

The only problem is :
Things that should be free and helpful to people, and basic things that normally would create a lot of on app engagements is completely locked behind a paywall.
All while the fee is pretty small and modest, and a fee applied to cosmetics does make sense as it doesn't negatively impact users experience, it doesn't really make sense to core elements like the different liquid options.

The app then becomes if anything a cutified version of any free and available program out there.
Sure the program is easy to use and does look great, but it doesn't really try to make itself any different in any other regard and the options that could come handy to make it unique is blocked outright by the paywall.

Applications such as Lifesum which are dieting managers does everything WaterLlama does without a fee (and without a cute mascot).

It does raise a few eyebrows about where the devs stands and it is kind of self aware all the whilst delusional.
When about to pay, if you change your mind you will be greeted with a screen telling you "Premium users are 91% more likely to stay hydrated!" 
Weirdly odd statistic, inaccurate and unclear sampling method, if anything maybe people simply deinstalled the app for a free experience without the mascot.

The applications is nothing but dubious at best.

title: If you have an eating disorder, don’t download this app!
text:
And I would also suggest that you read this even if you don’t have an eating disorder, before you decide whether or not you want to proceed with this. So, before I even start on my own issues with this app, let me explain why I raised the topic of eating disorders. 

I noticed a reviewer who had an eating disorder, who pointed out that some drinks are described as ‘evil’ in the app. This wasn’t the first complaint about that word. I’m beyond furious with the second half of the response by the team:
“We're sorry if [IF? That’s no way to start an apology! It should say ‘that it made’. ‘If’ implies that you don’t believe the reviewer!]… the labeling made you feel uncomfortable [UNCOMFORTABLE! Does the writer know anything at all about eating disorders?! It didn’t just make the reviewer uncomfortable, like they bought the wrong armchair. It set their recovery back considerably! They were very brave to raise this with the app owners, and even were kind enough to say lovely things about the app first!]—it's never our intention to set anyone back. We're all about promoting hydration and a balanced lifestyle [And clearly not all about how you affect people’s mental health]. Remember, the term "evil" is just a nudge to encourage healthier choices for overall well-being, the weight loss actually plays the least role in that. It's essential to focus on what makes you feel good, both physically and mentally.   
Feel free to do your own choices, and don't hesitate to consult with your doctor about what works best for you! Keep staying hydrated and enjoying those adorable characters! 😊” 
So that’s ok then. No genuine apology. Just, lighten up a bit about the word evil. You, the reviewer, are the one who should change your attitude. THAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE WHEN TALKING TO SOMEONE WITH AN EATING DISORDER! The reviewer should have received a full apology for the harm caused, and the word should have been removed straight away.  Also, whilst weight loss comments might be useful for many people, your attitude, app owners, should be along the lines of, ‘If you are overweight you might like to consider these facts’, not making too big a deal of it. And advising someone under these circumstances not to ‘hesitate to consult with your doctor about what works best with you’ is so insensitive and, again, shows ignorance when it comes to eating disorders. This app is designed to appeal to young people, so weight loss should be a topic mentioned with care and thought. If you think you handled it with care and thought, then you need to handle it with a lot more care and thought, consulting a specialist or doing A LOT of research. And the comments are utterly patronising. 
Had I seen this horrific reply before I bought the app, not only would I have not downloaded it, but I would have gone to Trust Pilot to see if I could leave a low rating there. I’ll still do that. 
Now my own review:
Positives - 
~It seemed to be the cheapest way to get the full use of the app, to pay the ‘for life’ premium, as it was ‘on offer’, but I still didn’t want to pay that much. As I backed away, they reduced the offer price by half, which seemed reasonable, if it worked. £8.99 (August 2026)
~There is a huge amount of information in the app, about drinking, not drinking enough, dehydration, the value of different kinds of drinks etc. I didn’t know, for example, that skimmed milk is more hydrating than water (the app added more ‘water’ to the daily count to allow for this, but I have no way to check if this adding to the total makes sense or is scientifically correct). It would take a long time to research for all the information that the app provides online, and most of us wouldn’t bother. 
Negatives - 
What a shambles! There is no clear help section, guiding people through all the different options. I was encouraged to enter my first drink, then given a choice for the size of the drink. It was 300ml, but I couldn’t enter that. I entered a false amount, and only then was I shown options to alter the amounts. I had skimmed milk, which I suspected would make a difference (I assumed it would be less hydrating) but I couldn’t enter that. Only later did skimmed milk make an appearance on the app. And so it went on. You can name drinks, but I can’t be sure that it always recognises them. After using the app for a few days, more details became available. It was irritating, but, having paid for it, I probably wouldn’t have persevered. Had there been an opportunity to try the app free for a fortnight, I would have given up and tried something else. 
As it is, I’m not happy using this app having seen such lack of disrespect and care when the owners have replied so badly to the review I have talked about here. So, even though I paid for it, I will be deleting it.

maker: Leo Mehlig and the Structured team / unorderly GmbH
title: Lacks Most Basic Functionalities
text:
I needed calendar integration, so I upgraded to a yearly subscription.  I utterly regretted 2 mins after starting using the app.  It lacks the most basic day-to-day functionalities one would expect from any task management app.  For starters, there is no search function whatsoever!  I couldn’t believe that until I got the confirmation from the help section of the developer’s own website.  NO SEARCH AND NO LIST VIEW.  This means you’d better REMEMBER every task you ever created.  God forbids, if you ever want to look up a specific task, you’ll actually need to flip through every day, one day at a time.  That ALONE would render the app completely useless.  But it gets worse.  There’s no “back to today” either.  You’ll literally have to pull up the calendar and find today’s date to click on.   And the whole flow to create a task is awkward too.  I created a few tasks without realizing the wrong date was selected.  Then afterwards, of course I couldn’t find them.  Remember, NO SEARCH and NO LIST VIEW!  I flipped through weeks worth of daily tasks to locate them.

I’m genuinely shocked at the overwhelmingly positive reviews for such an instantly laughably useless app.  I would say daily view, which is the only view, does look pleasing to the eyes.  I guess a lot of people have tons of time looking at a pretty planner and nothing important to do, because if they do have any real tasks, the planner isn’t going to help them accomplish them.

maker: Leo Mehlig and the Structured team / unorderly GmbH
title: Useful. However Causes Excess Battery Drain
text: Honestly, this is a really good application. I really love the UI and it’s pretty easy to use. I especially love how there is a Web version which allows me to use it for my day to day planning at work. Overall it’s intuitive and very good for people who like to stay organized and use daily planners. The one caveat with this application and the only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars (and also the reason I am on the fence about subscribing for it) is the battery drain on this app. It appears that this application has NOT been optimized AT ALL for battery efficiency. I am on the iPhone 17 Pro Max, my battery is fantastic. That said - THIS APP DRAINS IT. After several days of usage, I’ve been able to determine it drains about 0.36% of battery per minute. Which I mean, doesn’t seem like much at first glance. But when you run the math on it, that means just using this app for about 25ish minutes a day will drain 10% of your battery.. That’s a lot for a todo/daily planner application. The first day I got the app and I set up my schedule and all my repeating tasks, I used the app for about 1 hour and 5 minutes of screen on time, that resulted in 25% battery usage. To be blunt, that’s horrendously poor optimization. Just for perspective, highly resource intensive applications such as BlackMagic Camera when filming in 60 FPS at 4K use the EXACT SAME amount of battery as this application per minute. There is no reason a daily planner should drain just as much and sometimes more than a highly intensive and resource demanding video recording application. This should definitely be investigated.

maker: Leo Mehlig and the Structured team / unorderly GmbH
title: Day 2 of my trial and I’m NOT subscribing when it ends
text:
I really wanted to like Structured because it advertises itself as being especially helpful for people with ADHD. Unfortunately, my experience during the trial was the opposite.

The AI was the main reason I considered paying for the app, but it ended up creating more work instead of saving me time. I would ask it to schedule tasks, then have to go back and manually fix the schedule. When I asked it to move a multi-step outing (such as a library trip with walking there, signing up for library cards, browsing, and walking home), it only moved one task and left the others behind. That completely broke the plan and forced me to reorganize everything myself.

Recurring tasks were another major frustration. When I tried to delete a recurring task, I wasn’t given the expected options to delete just one occurrence, all future occurrences, or the entire series. Instead, I had to edit the recurrence before I could finally remove it. That’s confusing and unnecessarily time-consuming.

Importing Apple Reminders was another disappointing experience. I have well-organized reminder lists with headings, tasks, and subtasks. Structured completely flattened everything during the import, splitting headings, tasks, and subtasks into individual inbox items. Instead of preserving the organization, it created a cluttered mess.

To make matters worse, there was no way to select those imported items as a group and hide or remove them. I had to tap each one individually. The only workaround I found was going into the app’s settings and manually disabling each Reminders list one by one. Even then, one of the lists continued appearing in my inbox after it had been turned off. I had to repeatedly enable and disable the list before Structured finally removed those items.

The app also advertises swipe gestures to quickly delete, postpone, or manage tasks, but those gestures didn’t work for me at all.

After spending my trial fighting with the AI, fixing broken schedules, cleaning up imported reminders, and manually reorganizing tasks, I realized I could accomplish the same thing by using Apple Calendar alongside Reminders. The AI was supposed to be the feature that justified the subscription, but in my experience it wasn’t reliable enough to do that.

The concept behind Structured is excellent, and I can see why people are excited about it. However, the current AI and task management experience simply wasn’t dependable enough for me to trust with my daily planning. Instead of reducing my mental load, it increased it.

maker: Leo Mehlig and the Structured team / unorderly GmbH
title: I LOVE This App, but the Inbox Is HORRIBLY PAINFUL! Please end the suffering!
text:
I absolutely love this app except for one thing: The Inbox.

If it wasn’t for the inbox, I would give this app five stars. In fact, I would give it more if I could.

The Inbox is so painful to use on a tablet and especially on a phone if you have a lot of items sitting there that you haven’t scheduled yet. And isn’t that the whole point of an inbox? I put things there because I know I need to do them, I don’t want to forget them, but I don’t necessarily know yet when I’m going to do them.

I currently have around 20 things in my Inbox, and trying to organize them is incredibly frustrating. You have to press and hold each task and drag it where you want it. But if you’re trying to move something farther up the list, once you reach the top of the screen, IT DOESN’T KEEP SCROLLING. It just stops. So you have to let go of the task, scroll the list to make more room at the top, find the task again, drag it farther up, and keep repeating this process.

Why???

There’s also no way to filter or sort the Inbox by category, which would at least make managing a larger Inbox easier.

What frustrates me so much is that I genuinely LOVE this app. I have a lot of plates spinning in my life, with both big and little things I need to remember, and Structured is exactly the kind of app I need. But I’m starting to wonder if the Inbox is actually helping me manage all of those things or just giving me another frustrating list that I have to manage.

Please fix this user experience. At the very least, tasks should continuously scroll when you drag them to the top or bottom of the screen. Even better, give us ways to sort, filter, group, or otherwise organize the Inbox.

I design software, so I understand that development takes time and priorities have to be made. But this feels like such a fundamental usability issue in a core part of the app. Please make it a priority.

I really don’t want to stop using Structured because I love almost everything else about it. But the Inbox is making me want to.

maker: Frederik Riedel and team / riedel.wtf apps S.L.
title: Strong blocking, but missing real accountability
text:
This app does a good job enforcing Screen Time limits, but it falls short as an accountability tool.

Like most Screen Time apps, it relies on three mechanisms:
	•	app time limits
	•	unlocks / temporary access
	•	scheduled blocks

The problem is that following or breaking these rules isn’t meaningfully tracked. Users can:
	•	repeatedly use unlocks
	•	change limits or schedules after enforcement starts
	•	revoke Screen Time permissions and re-enable later

…without any persistent history or consequence inside the app. That makes it easy to undermine your own rules quietly, which defeats the purpose for serious users.

What would make this a 5-star app:
	•	an accountability history (unlock usage, schedule adherence, rule changes)
	•	logging Screen Time permission revocations/restores
	•	an integrity metric (did I keep my word or not)
	•	brief, optional reflection prompts at key moments (before unlocks, after rule changes)
	•	weekly summaries focused on accountability, not just usage minutes
	•	a place to define and revisit why you’re limiting apps, so behavior change is internal, not just enforced

Blocking alone changes behavior temporarily.
Accountability, integrity tracking, and reflection change it long-term.

If these additions were made, this would easily be a 5-star app.

title: For developer: missing a lot, please read everything
text:
Correct me if Im misunderstanding anything. This is coming from a developer of multiple years

first of all let’s start off with how almost every single feature is paid. I know that the you developers need the payment to continue working on it well, but some features that are behind a paywall are GENUINELY necessities that shouldn’t cost a dollar. For example you can’t even intervention block more than a single app without getting the subscription, and if you tested the app well you would know that most people need to block more than 1 app. Surprise surprise if TikTok is blocked I’ll just switch to Insta.

second I shouldn’t have to create a shortcuts automation every time I add an app to one sec. other focus apps allow you to block multiple apps in seconds. “linking” an app twice for each block/intervention is a bit redundant, it should just let me choose what apps i wanna block from a list. 

then there’s the fact there’s very little securing of your blocks unless you pay. it’s TOO easy to just delete the Shortcuts Automation to stop the app blocking forever, or just use the TikTok.com instead of the TikTok app (cause strict blocking is paid too…)

It’s also REALLY annoying how a bug fix was turned into a Pro feature (Intentional App Switching). Normally if you got timed out from an app, you would close the app for 5 minutes, take a break, and come back after 5 minutes. Well with one sec you have to wait the full 5 minutes INSIDE the app to be able to use it again, or you’ll have to wait for the timeout to expire every, single time you reopen the app. Only way to fix this? get pro which is stupid 

The last straw was when the stupid intervention feature wasn’t working properly at all. I needed to use YouTube for an emergency but every time I went through the intervention YouTube was still blocked. Don’t make so many features paid if the basic ones aren’t even working properly.

Developer, correct me if I misunderstood anything but in my opinion it’s not the most effective and a bit cash grabby. there are other focus apps like Opal with the same features for free

title: Inaccurate, all about the looks
text:
I have MECFS and struggle with pacing, especially with exercise — I usually end up giving myself post exertional malaise if I’m not extra careful (PEM). I was excited that this app boasted it was designed for chronic illness and pacing, and I’m pretty disappointed. 

I have two apps including this one that measure HRV, heart rate, recovery, etc. to help me use metrics to guide my pacing and decide if I should workout or stay in bed (or something in between). My other app always clocks my changes in these metrics and warns about systemic exertion or distress. This app ALMOST ALWAYS still tells me to workout. For those who don’t know, working out during PEM can cause mitochondrial damage, so this app— in my opinion — should not be in charge of anyone’s pacing or health. 

It’s a good start. It’s got a cool design and it syncs nice with the watches, etc. but the main purpose of helping chronically ill individuals take back control of their health and activity is defeated when the app is encouraging us to workout when our bodies are producing metrics that clearly say we shouldn’t, and the app can’t read that accurately. If anyone was using this solely, and trusted it completely, they could risk further mitochondrial damage and disease progression with the inaccuracies I’ve been facing. 

Even worse, the longer I used the app, the worse it got.

Dev feedback: camera HRV/HR reader in the morning in place of missing or bugged sleep data — or for extra confirmation

maker: Gentler Stories; Katarina Lotric, co-founder and CEO
title: Great start!
text:
It’s definitely a healthier approach than apple’s “close your rings everyday” approach. I bought the annual subscription and use the widget to keep keep an eye on my zones throughout the week. It’s a newer app, so I’m sure there’s a lot of great features on the way. After using it for few months here are my notes for improvement: 1. The app almost always says I’m overreaching. I’ve been working out 3x a week for one hour each morning doing moderate - intense weight training g. This has been my routine for months and it still says I’m pushing too hard. Perhaps add a way to adjust zones or customize it based on goals. 2. The zones seem arbitrary. As a user I have absolutely no clue how the graph is calculated or how the data I’m plugging in actually impacts future projections. Adding some reading material for us to reference that gets into the nitty gritty aspects of your algorithm would be helpful. 3. Analyze past Apple Health data/ allow back scrolling by more than 10 days. This might already be done, but that’s not apparent. Another benefit would include automatically giving personalized zones. 4. Minor but an Apple Watch-style ring closing notifications that tell me if I’m on track would be neat. I originally switched to replace that feature. Overall this is a great app and the UI is on point. The algorithm discourages pushing myself to the point of it almost being negative (coincidentally this leads me to ignore the “overreaching” alerts). However I feel it’s taught me to listen to my body more. I’m excited to see what your team has in store!

UPDATE
I appreciate the response. I have been using my Apple Watch for 18 months consistently, and gradually increased my workout with a personal trainer. Therefore the “overworking” algorithm appears to have bugs (cited by others, not just me.)
Since writing the review I have decided to switch back to Apple’s native health app. While the daily rings isn’t ideal, it offers a more robust analysis of my workout patterns. I look forward to trying Gentler Streak in the future when some more features have been added!

title: The app sucks SO MUCH since the update.
text:
Removal of streaming option was a dealbreaker for me because I like to listen to podcasts during my ~40min subway commute. During that commute I typically have 2-3 bars of reception when I'm at a station and 0 when I'm between them. With 'streaming', the app would download a bit more of the episode every time I was at a station and keep on playing, so my listening would be uninterrupted for my whole journey. 

Now that the option has been removed, I have to remember to pre-download several episodes before heading down to the subway. Otherwise, if an episode ends when l'm between stations, I need to wait till I get to the next one before I can start downloading another episode. Given that my reception at stations isn't super strong, the downloads often don't finish before the train pulls away again which results in a failed download and I have to sit in silence and wait for the next station before I can try again. I can sometimes pass through 2 or 3 stations before an episode downloads successfully.
It's utterly destroyed the listening experience for me.

Oh, and playlists are all messed up. 

Cancelled my Overcast subscription, deleted the app and started using Pocketcast instead which is vastly superior to this garbage fire of an update.

title: The new update ruined the app
text:
The new update has ruined a wonderful app. I’ve used Overcast for nine years — it used to be the best podcast app by a country mile.

This new update has somehow made every aspect of it worse:
Playlists have been moved to the top row, which makes them difficult to select.
The dev completely removed the ability to stream podcasts.
Almost every interaction now requires multiple more taps, like changing settings, or activating the sleep timer.
You can no longer set a custom sleep timer.
The search function is less useful.
The skip forward/backwards buttons have been removed from the Home Screen (requiring another additional tap).
Some downloads just don’t work.
Some episodes need to be downloaded twice??
The dev has removed the ability to delete multiple episodes at once, requiring the laborious process of doing every single one individually.

It’s a disaster. And such a shame. For the first time in almost a decade, I’m looking for another podcast app. Do not recommend.

title: This app used to be great for offline playing
text:
The redesign has changed some specific aspects of the app that used to make it great, particularly when it comes to downloading apps. Previously you could do a simple left swipe to quick-access the download button for a particular podcast episode - now this action requires three clicks into a menu, which you have to repeat for each episode. Especially considering the streaming ability was removed (for justifiable reasons) this is baffling. Ease of downloading for offline playing was the killer feature of Overcast for me, and this adds a lot of friction to that.

The information panel for podcasts is less accessible now too. Instead of accessing with a swipe as previously, you have to click an icon button at the top of the screen. Not a big deal, but why change what worked? Especially when you could access the info panel with one hand previously - now it’s in a high enough spot you need two.

Apparently the auto-delete bug has been fixed, so that’s not an issue any more, but this release really seems to have been half-baked. I guess that’s good it’s better on the backend, but frankly the user cares far less about that than you do!

title: Many bugs still after rewrite which don’t seem to be being fixed in favour of niche bells & whistles
text:
* Ranked High-Priority and Date orders are frequently ignored when new episodes are inserted to smart playlists, with episodes inserted in an arbitrary order into the playlist (I have recent screenshots from the many recent times I’ve reported this in TestFlight, in-app, and on a couple of occasions Mastadon). 
* Similarly an excluded High-Priority episode that is added back to the playlist is always added to the top, not by its Ranked High-Priority order. 
* Newly subscribed podcast episodes are inserted above High-Priority episodes when they are initially added to the playlist, should be below High-Priority list. 
* Resuming playback will sometimes not resume the previously playing episode and will instead play the next episode by priority (gets that bit correct, at least!). 
* Playback sometimes does not pause when removing AirPods. 
* Overcast does not show in Now Playing widget on Lock Screen after connecting to audio device e.g. AirPods, other Bluetooth audio device.
* Overcast sometimes does not play through CarPlay, requiring the app to be quit and reopened on the iPhone (though this may be a CarPlay bug, or at least this same issue exists in Spotify).
* Current Podcast list no longer shows podcasts with played episodes which have not been deleted (this was Overcast’s previous behaviour and also the way the Podcast information page still works).
* The horizontal playlist carousel looks bad more than ~3 playlists. 
* The horizontal playlist carousel is functionally poor with more than ~3 playlists.
* Downloads do not always happen in the background - I will receive a notification for an episode, open it some time after receiving it, and the episode shows Waiting to Download.
* On the Add Podcast screen, tapping the description text does not expand this to show the full text where it is truncated.

This was & can still be a good app but the radio silence & self-satisfied stance towards ongoing issues is not okay.

Yesterday, I received a phone call while listening to ATP.fm (the irony) and after the call ended, Overcast simply never resumed playback and my now playing widget showed that I was listening to nothing. I’ve witnessed this behavior a lot frequently where if the podcast is paused, for a min or longer, the now playing widget shows nothing playing and I have to open the app and resume playback. It’s like the process is being backgrounded and killed. 

This is a podcast app, it should play audio seamlessly and effortlessly like Apple Music, the Apple Podcast app, and even backgrounded YouTube. It doesn’t. 

The developer whines on his podcasts about how bad the negative reviews make him feel. I too develop software used by random people across the globe. I take the feedback and improve the product I work on. I don’t whine to my podcast audience about how negative feedback hurts my feelings, I fix the issues.

For podcasts with daily episodes, this is an absolute nightmare. I had a 1-3 episode limit for these, and I could just manually pick the ones I wanted instead of filling up my storage. However that’s not possible now, and even just a few days of this update has added over 1gb to my storage. 

There have also been some pretty annoying changes with previous updates too. For instance, if a specific episode has custom episode art, the title is pushed over to the right. Titles without custom art are justified all the way to the left. This means you can’t easily scroll a list, because the titles are now essentially in two different columns. 

I totally get that it’s just one person making this, so I know that can occasionally come with hiccups, but I’m just so confused how decisions are being made for such a popular app. It feels like the developer is just making choices based on HIS own podcasts, not what others use it for. 

I’m pretty sure something from every new update recently has had to be rolled back or fixed, which doesn’t reflect very well on however decisions are being made. 

I’ve worked in tech for years, and UX/UI testing is really crucial, even for small teams of developers. There are some pretty avoidable mistakes that keep happening that it seems like would have been caught from user testing. 

The benefits of using the app now are outweighed by the negative, which is really disappointing. I hope this episode limit change gets rolled back because otherwise I literally won’t have the phone storage to keep listening to podcasts on this app, which feels crazy to me.

title: The mighty has fallen
text:
TLDR: find another app. I was a power user with things, but it no longer fits my needs. 

I never thought I’d write this. Things has always been the best. Always the sharpest looking. Always ready for productivity. Always in Apple’s spotlight. But Things has been slowing down…

Today, iOS 26 launched. I woke up hopeful that Things would surprise us by giving us a new feature. Maybe a new UI refresh. Nope. Their update was a barebones update to stay “current”. A glass icon and a glassy like plus button. Wooo thanks! 

I have bought every version of things. The visionOS release was strike one. A full price for a multi year app that just has translucent sidebars? Come on. I messaged the devs many times asking what most of us are asking and needing: attachment support, better markdown (the current setup is insanely stupid), collaboration, or even a refreshed coat of paint to not look like an older app. The responses we get? Thanks for the feedback, we aren’t doing it. 

Today, I’m uninstalling things. This big update from them is a joke. To the other devs who listen and keep the magic of Apple software release day still magical, thank you. To Cultured Code, thanks for the great years ranging all the way back to Things 1. You’ve lost your touch, your magic. I hope you find it again and find joy in your work.

title: Devil's advocate
text:
The new Things is clearly a powerful and sleek beast . I haven't though seen many reviews of Things iOS that mention downsides . I do wonder how anyone can assess a new app thoroughly enough to confidently award 5 stars, within days of its release . To perhaps redress the balance (or is it an 'outpouring of negativity'), here are my rough jottings of aspects of Things 3 that I find a turn off:
Loss of functionality from Things 2 as listed in the Things Support article e.g. Projects list gone, can no longer set an advance warning of a deadline, can no longer filter by 'no tag', nor by deadline, cannot change font size, no time stamp inside to-dos. Plus:
No alphabetical sort of projects in sidebar
No collapsing of areas in "sidebar "
Spotlight integration is gone.
Additionally:
No collapsing of the new headings within projects 
Loss of shading impedes ease of the "form filling " aspect of using the app. Things 2 had a superb UI design, attractive and guiding  the user 's eye. We now have white space 
Loss of colour coding of areas - no green icons, except in Someday 
No location-based to dos 
Still no repeating to dos in projects 
Too much white space on the screen ( see above). It's harsh on the eye and creates glare.
Things 3 "What's new" says " When you open a to-do, it smoothly transforms into a clear white piece of paper, ready for your thoughts. " A blank canvas may be helpful if I'm writing a book or a journal, but Things is essentially a database and I find the structure of a form helpful when entering data.
Notes still cannot be hidden
No undo or cancel button e.g. Creating a new to do
I have difficulty in moving around the app - I'm not finding it intuitive 
You can't switch to landscape view  (being locked in portrait feels claustrophobic to me)
The new 'headings' feature looks quite useful, but what is its intended purpose? If it's really defining a sub-task, why can't you mark it 'done'?
The checklist feature is rather in the same category. Nifty, but isn't it really a sub-task? I can't figure out how to archive a checklist for future use, a feature that would be very handy and would justify the use of the term 'checklist'.
The very useful improvements and new features of Things 3 have probably all been covered in the avalanche of positive reviews, so I won't mention them here. It is a good app in many ways , but a long way (in my view) from being brilliant . It is a surprise to me that I much prefer Things 2! Having said that, my 2 star marking is tongue-in-cheek - or just plain cheek! - the app is much better than that. But when you're the devil's advocate, needs must😊. I hope the developer will enhance and improve the features of Things 3, to build on the excellent work they have already done.

title: Excellent App but needs critical improvement to avoid being money sink
text:
I would readily pay all $80 the developers want from us for this app suite! It is overall excellent and exactly what I was looking for in a to-do app. However, when I purchase a suite such as this, I assume that I will be able to use it at its current level of functionality for several years -- to put it on the same price level as $30/year subscription services like its peers. When things 3 came out, the developers dropped support for syncing in things 2! This is absolutely unacceptable as if I didn't want syncing I would not pay the extra $30 for the iPhone and iPad apps. I do not expect the developers to maintain expensive servers indefinitely, however. 

The developers need to add support for syncing over iCloud like most other syncing apps on the App store, or my rating will remain low as I expect upon the advent of things 4, sync support will once again be dropped. This would allow users to use the $80 software suite that they paid for for as long as they choose, and purchase the new version if they feel the features so warrant it, not because the developers feel as though it is appropriate to extort users by disrupting their use of the existing software.

title: Recreate Subtasks Manually? Really?!
text:
It’s really absurd that it’s impossible to convert tasks into subtasks. For years I’ve tried to embrace Things into my workflow, but every time I get back to using it I get reminded immediately why I’d never used it for longer than a week before.

If I have any number of tasks 3, 8, 15.. and I decide to convert them into subtasks i.e. group them within a single parent task, there is no way to do so.

It wouldn’t even import subtasks from Reminders!
All reminders subtasks get imported as individual tasks, and I have to manually copy tens of tasks one by one and paste them as tasks one by one.

What an awful and unpleasant experience.

It’s really incredible how such a wonderful and powerful app gets completely crippled by this flaw that renders it unusable to me. I have Things installed on my iPhone, iPad, Mac & Apple Watch. Just sitting pretty collecting digital dust because it’s a productivity nightmare.

I wish the developers would reconsider & deliver this essential feature as an update in a near future. There are paid users like myself that have nought every version of this up & haven’t gotten their money’s worth from the app.

title: Another subscription?
text:
I know it isn’t much, but I don’t like the idea of a subscription for a weather app. Especially one that keeps trying to trick you into one. If you think that isn’t fair… read on. 

Features like “customize layout” or “change icon” are fine to be paid features. I have no issue with that. What is annoying is that the app will let you get to the setting first and then when you go to apply it it will tell you that it’s a paid feature. The UI is intentionally misleading and very frustrating as a first-time user. 

Gray out the setting entirely and put a lock icon by it. By not doing this it makes it feel like any value is behind a paywall. I know the whole deal is that weather data isn’t free. I understand that. But then why is that the only free feature in the app? I’m fine to pay for longer forecasts or stuff like that. Or even timely weather notifications. But to add a widget? Or to change an icon? Come on. I need to pay a subscription to change an icon? How is that worth $40 a year?

I am not opposed to paying for apps. I bought Dark Sky, but also appreciated that it was a one-time purchase. If this app wants to appeal to a wider audience, it needs to make some basic tweaks. I’ve heard a lot of great reviews for this app, but this experience left me severely disappointed. Not the first time I’ve tried the app either.

2) Notifications are not reliable on Apple Watch. I only get a 2 notifications per day on a task with 5 sub tasks. 
3) If I complete all sub tasks early in the day, I still get notifications later in the day. Having the ability to add a notification time per sub task might help solve this as the notifications would not be completely separate from the tasks themselves. 
4) I can’t figure out how to edit a future task. I can only edit tasks that are scheduled for the current day. 

I love the idea of this app but it is missing a huge amount of polish.

title: Great concept, unreliable sync
text:
The Streaks app offers a fantastic concept for habit tracking, but its execution falls short. Synchronisation between the Apple Watch, iPhone, and Mac is frustratingly unreliable. Tasks completed on the Apple Watch frequently fail to update on other devices, and activity ring progress doesn’t show correctly on the watch. Likewise Mac or iPhone to the watch. 

This is particularly disappointing given that iCloud sync is enabled on all devices, background app refresh is on, and the devices are connected to fast, reliable Wi-Fi. Considering the small amount of data being transferred when a task is completed, the sync issues are difficult to excuse.

Support was unhelpful, even infering they don’t have an Apple Watch for testing. While the idea is solid, the app's poor sync and lack of refinement make it hard to recommend in its current state.

Review besides the bug below:

The concept of streaks is really solid to form habits. It’s a psychological hack, yes, but something that works for me. Mind you an app is not as powerful as a poster in a room, but its the next best thing.

I have had a few apps which track streaks, and this app, Streaks, definitely has the best design that actually is close to checking out things on a poster. And UI really is important to promote usage and habit building.

The cool things which this app does differently which stood out for me:
1: you can set timers for timed activities like 1 hour study or 15 min meditation.
2. Multiple tasks which form an activity can be broken down. For e.g, drinking 10 glasses of water can be checked off one glass at a time.
3. There’s a tie in to health app so you don’t need to check off workouts and other health things.

Overall happy with this app and see myself using it. I have had a few streaks going the last couple of months, but have not been consistent enough. Hope that will change in the coming months.

title: More screens is a must for some users
text:
I appreciate the ideal of focusing on only 12 habits and can see that some UI currently hinges on the two screens. But it feels arbitrary to not have the option to add additional screens if I need them, and the option would do no harm to anyone that can manage with the default two screens.

Alongside other habits, I wanted to track weekly streaks for running, cycling and swimming targets, but tracking their streaks individually uses up a quarter of all my slots. Why should someone that runs three days a week have more other habit slots to track with than someone that does three different exercises per week? I also wanted to track sleep as when I go to bed and when I wake up, rather than just overall time so I can see where I’m missing my targets. I find that habits work for me when I can focus on specific details, but I’m having to generalise or cut other things out to make space.

I really like the way the app works in general, and to be honest I’d pay for additional screens or a second instance of the same app just to track what I want. Compromising on what details I can track is a real frustration though, and I do regret paying for it at the moment rather than finding an app with no limits. I’ve already spent time setting up shortcuts and some habits so I’ll cross my fingers for an improvement while I test out other apps for a secondary/replacement tracker.
